# v3.2.0

*Published on September 3, 2026.*
<!-- END AUTO-GENERATED -->

<!-- BEGIN SUMMARY (contributors: edit freely; preserved on re-run) -->

## Summary

Jupyter AI v3.2.0 refactors the entire stack to make real-time collaboration (RTC) optional, and removes `jupyter-server-documents` (JSD) as a required dependency. The default distribution (`jupyter-ai`) will no longer require RTC moving forwards. AI personas are still able to edit, run, and debug notebooks in real-time, with or without RTC.


This release is largely a refactor that fixes the various bugs reported by users and admins following the v3.0 official release, many of which have been tied to JSD and its RTC implementation. Aside from a more reliable and stable experience, user-facing changes are intended to be minimal.

Jupyter AI will continue to support RTC as an optional integration point, with either `jupyter-collaboration` or JSD. Users interested in using Jupyter AI with RTC should install one of the two new optional dependency groups:

- `jupyter-ai[rtc]` - `jupyter-ai` with `jupyter-collaboration`
- `jupyter-ai[rtc-jsd]` - `jupyter-ai` with `jupyter-server-documents`


### New `jupyter-live-content`

A new package, `jupyter-live-content`, has been introduced to update the UI in response to file changes on disk. Agent edits to `.py` and `.md` files, for example, are always immediately reflected in the browser, even without RTC. This fixes a real gap in the default JupyterLab experience, and we will work with other maintainers to upstream this project.

This extension is automatically disabled when RTC is installed and enabled, since this capability is already provided by RTC.

Two caveats worth mentioning:

1. Notebooks are *not* updated in real time when their contents change on disk. Supporting this reliably requires a robust design that needs more review and testing.

2. Scroll position is lost when the file UI refreshes. We are aware of this usability issue and will work to address it in subsequent releases.


Note that agents and AI personas in the Jupyter AI chat panel are still able to edit and run notebooks in real-time. This is described in more detail below.

### Refactored chat backend

This release upgrades to Jupyter Chat v0.25.0, which also removes its dependency on RTC. It now ships its own WebSocket protocol that is used when RTC is not installed in the environment. Thank you [@brichet](https://github.com/brichet) for building the initial implementation and testing all of the subsequent changes on short notice!

When RTC is installed and enabled, the server extension falls back to the original `YChat` implementation used before v3.2.0. We are still exploring whether having two different server-side chat models is necessary moving forwards.

### Refactored tools

The MCP tools provided by Jupyter AI have all been refactored to work without RTC. AI personas are still able to edit, run, and debug notebooks in real-time without RTC by calling JupyterLab frontend commands provided by `jupyterlab-ai-commands`. This is the same set of tools used in Jupyterlite AI.

When RTC is installed and enabled, the tools fall back to the original implementation that relied on RTC APIs, used before v3.2.0.

We have also fixed a major bug where tool calls powered by JupyterLab frontend commands were run on all browsers connected to the server. This has now been fixed, and tool calls that run JupyterLab frontend commands are only run on the browser which sent the message triggering them.

### Thank you

Thank you to everyone who helped report bugs, review proposals, test pre-releases, fix bugs, refactor code, and share feedback! This release would not have been possible without the support of the community.

<!-- END SUMMARY -->
